ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 3. WHAT CHANGED SINCE CYCLE 13 AND WHY IT DID NOT MOVE THE NUMBER: cycle 13's rationale said the single thing standing between this issue and a stronger footing was that src-0007 bore directly on it but had never been attached to the graph, so the STATE recorded only a two-source claim and a T4 could not create a three-source claim by asserting it in a rationale. Cycle 16 attached it: there is now a second supported candidate_resolution with evidence [src-0007, src-0002] carrying ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.1771/0.1414 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini), all nine figures re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 to four decimal places. So the deficit cycle 13 named is discharged and the floor under this 3 is materially firmer than it was: the primary claim now rests on three unaffiliated teams (src-0002 CTIBench, src-0005 CyberSOCEval, src-0007 CyberThreat-Eval) rather than two, and src-0007 supplies a within-table control that cross-benchmark synthesis cannot -- identical models, identical corpus, identical harness reaching 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, so the ATT&CK deficit cannot be blamed on corpus difficulty or prompt quality. THAT IS A BETTER 3, NOT A 4. The rubric's level-4 bar is counterarguments explicitly ADDRESSED, and the counterargument that matters most here is unchanged and now in its tenth cycle of being merely listed: open_question[1] asks for a human-analyst baseline F1 for ATT&CK technique extraction, and without it we cannot say whether 0.64 (or 0.28) is near or far from what a human analyst achieves on the same material. Every number in this issue is an absolute score with no human reference point, so 'hard, unsolved sub-task' is an interpretation of those numbers rather than a demonstrated comparison. Adding a third source measuring the same thing does not address that; it makes the unanchored measurement more reliable without anchoring it. Cycle 16 did partially answer open_question[2] in the negative -- fine-tuning makes this sub-task WORSE (0.2787/0.2270 falling to 0.2387/0.1846 for fine-tuned GPT-4o), echoing src-0001 -- but narrowing an open question is not the same as addressing a counterargument. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED: src-0005's per-model numeric scores have never been captured in twelve cycles (carry-forward [10], the oldest un-actioned collection task in the project); cycle 9's G2 confirmed its claims in substance but explicitly NOT verbatim, so one of the sources under candidate 1 remains the weakest-verified in the base. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 2, and this is the least changed issue in the graph -- no source has been added to it, no candidate has changed status, and its last attempt was cycle 9, ten cycles ago. Structure is unchanged and is the textbook shape of a level 2: candidate 1 (LANCE 97.6% F1 against the manually-validated 1,791-IoC PRISM benchmark, versus legacy baselines IoC Searcher+whitelist 76%, AlienVault OTX 72%, VirusTotal@threshold=1 86%) rests on src-0003 ALONE; candidate 2 (vanilla-LLM precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1310 expert-annotated IoCs from a production workflow) rests on src-0007 ALONE; the only multi-source candidate, the scaffolding-not-the-model synthesis with evidence [src-0003, src-0007, src-0008], is deliberately held at 'proposed' because no source tests it. The rubric's bar for 3 is that the PRIMARY candidate be supported by at least two independent sources, not that the issue accumulate two sources -- and src-0003 and src-0007 do not jointly support one claim, they pull in opposite directions on magnitude, which is precisely why ctr-0001 exists. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC, STATED SEPARATELY SO IT IS AUDITABLE. Pre-gate score on the merits = 2. ctr-0001 (opened cycle 9, resolved_cycle null) is the graph's ONLY open contradiction and it is filed against this issue. I applied the CEILING reading: the score may not exceed scale_max minus g3_contradiction_demotion = 5 - 2 = 3. THE CEILING DID NOT BIND -- the merit score of 2 is already below 3, so the gate changed nothing this cycle, and no demotion was applied to any other issue. WHICH READING AND WHY, for the fifth consecutive assessment: prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 and config.yml line 35's comment both specify a SUBTRACTION (lose 2, floor 0), while scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 implements a CEILING and errors only if score > 3. The enforced reading is in the minority, and the divergence is silent if left unfixed, because subtraction produces LOWER scores that never trip the validator's check. Cycle 16 ruled for the ceiling on the ground that the rubric is definitional rather than arithmetic -- its levels define evidential states (0 = 'no candidate resolutions', 1 = 'no supported resolution'), so subtracting 2 from an honest 2 would stamp this issue with a label that is factually false of it (it has three candidate_resolutions, two of them supported) and would hand the weakest-link selector a fabricated bottom. Cycles 10, 11 and 13 applied the ceiling and so does this cycle. T4 has no standing to reconcile the specifications by editing prompts/, config.yml or scripts/; the replacement text for both artefacts is in logs/cycle-016.md 'Item 3' and awaits a human. Carried forward as [4]. WHAT WOULD MOVE THIS: ctr-0001's three confounds are all still unresolved -- SYSTEM (LANCE is regex pre-filter + LLM + human validation; src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs'), METRIC (97.6% F1 versus precision-only, with cycle 15's whole-table pull confirming no recall or F1 row for IoC extraction exists anywhere in that table), and CORPUS (50 public threat reports versus an unnamed company's internal daily workflow). Cycle 18 narrowed the METRIC confound specifically: an IoC recall low enough to reconcile the two sources by metric artefact alone would have to be 0.09-0.15, which no source reports for report-level extraction, so the metric explanation is weaker than the system explanation. That makes ctr-0001 MORE likely to dissolve into the scaffolding candidate, but nobody has run the resolution path (recover recall/F1 from src-0007's released code on GitHub/HuggingFace, or find a head-to-head), so it stays open and the score stays at 2.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: HELD AT 2, and this is the hardest hold in this assessment because the issue has genuinely improved without becoming scoreable higher. THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT: both SUPPORTED candidate_resolutions cite evidence [src-0001] and nothing else, and the rubric's level 3 requires the PRIMARY candidate to be supported by at least two independent sources. A second candidate that sharpens the first using the same source is not a second source. WHAT CHANGED: cycle 15's T1 added four sources measuring these axes -- src-0013 (calibration, ECE/Brier on secure code generation), src-0014 (prompt-sensitivity and abstention on vulnerability detection), src-0015 (action-threshold calibration for incident-response agents), src-0016 (same-input repeat-query stability on JavaScript SAST) -- and they are attached here as candidate 3, correctly at status 'proposed'. Cycle 16's T2 then made an explicit SCOPE RULING, recorded as candidate 4, declining to treat security-adjacent corroboration as CTI multi-source support. I ENDORSE THAT RULING RATHER THAN RE-LITIGATING IT, and note the reason it is right is not pedantry: this issue's whole content is that CTI reliability has axes beyond accuracy, and every one of the four new sources measures a NON-CTI task (code generation, CVE code samples, synthetic IR episodes, JavaScript fixtures). Promoting on them would be asserting the very generalisation across task domains that the parent issue treats as an open question. So the direction of the phenomenon is now corroborated four ways and the CTI-specific claim is still single-source. That is exactly a 2. THIS CYCLE'S G2 BEARS DIRECTLY ON THIS ISSUE AND IS RECORDED HERE: I re-verified src-0014 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.24171) and it PASSED, with strengthening. Every body figure stored for it was returned verbatim and exact -- cross-strategy F1 range 0.398 for Gemma (0.102 under A-CoT to 0.499 under self-consistency) against 0.103 for Mistral; CoT mean F1 0.465, mean effective F1 0.427, mean abstention 7.28%; A-CoT recall collapse CodeLlama 0.685 to 0.279, Falcon 0.541 to 0.223, Gemma 0.420 to 0.057, Mistral 0.423 to 0.280; 6,074 code samples from 1,000 CVEs. Beyond re-confirmation, I pulled Tables 2 and 3 whole for the first time (carry-forward [20] discharged for this source) and obtained an INDEPENDENT CONSISTENCY CHECK the stored claims did not have: the five stored coverage figures are exact arithmetic complements of Table 2's self-consistency abstention column, all five to the second decimal -- CodeLlama 100 - 49.00 = 51.00, Mistral 100 - 51.07 = 48.93, Gemma 100 - 39.15 = 60.85, DeepSeek 100 - 60.96 = 39.04, Falcon 100 - 75.96 = 24.04 -- and Table 3's CoT and A-CoT recall columns reproduce all four stored recall-collapse pairs cell for cell. Table-level confirmation of a body sentence by a different route is the strongest form of verification available to this loop, and src-0014 now has it. It still does not raise this score, because verification quality is orthogonal to source count and src-0014 is not CTI. ONE NEW OBSERVATION FROM THE PULL, recorded because no cycle had it: Table 3's precision ranges are 0.487-0.531 (DeepSeek), 0.499-0.517 (Mistral), 0.488-0.646 (Gemma), 0.492-0.517 (Falcon) and 0.491-0.495 (CodeLlama) -- i.e. precision sits near 0.5 for every model under every prompting strategy on a binary task. That is a substantive limit on how much any of src-0014's F1 movement can mean, and a future cycle citing this source should carry it. It is an observation about an already-collected source, not a new claim requiring a new citation. ALL FOUR open_questions remain wholly unaddressed. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment. SELECTOR NOTE: this issue is tied at 2 with ioc-extraction-reliability and automated-triage-under-refusal, but its attempts are [3, 15, 16] -- two of them inside the five-cycle penalty window (cycles 15 and 16 against a current cycle of 19, window floor 14) -- so at tie_break_recent_attempt_penalty of 1 per attempt it carries a penalty of 2 and should NOT be the selector's pick.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: HELD AT 3. The primary candidate rests on two genuinely independent sources of different kinds, both attached: src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-TAA over 50 real reports, where every one of five tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate exceeds its correct rate -- GPT-4-turbo 86% plausible against 52% correct, Gemini-1.5 74% against 38%) and src-0004 (Heise reporting Der Spiegel on ENISA's APT29/Midnight Blizzard misattribution published in an official report). An academic benchmark plus investigative reporting on a production incident is the real independence that separates this issue from the single-source 2s. WHAT CHANGED SINCE CYCLE 13: cycle 16 added a second candidate carrying src-0007's Table 4 'Content: Threat Actor' rubric block -- GPT-4o 1.547 Relevance / 1.528 Accuracy / 1.140 Attribution against o3-mini 3.964 / 3.656 / 2.968 on the same task, corpus and rubric. Its load-bearing element is the within-table contrast rather than the model gap: the same GPT-4o scores 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.612 on 'Content: Root Cause' in the same table, so 1.140 on threat-actor attribution is a deficit specific to attribution rather than a general inability to draft -- the same shape as src-0002's finding by a different instrument. THAT CANDIDATE IS CORRECTLY AT 'proposed' AND I AM NOT COUNTING IT AS A THIRD LEG, for the two reasons recorded at its entry and which I re-read rather than took on trust: (1) the GPT-4o (FT) column reads 3.964 / 3.655 / 2.967 against o3-mini's 3.964 / 3.656 / 2.968, identical to within 0.001 on all three rows, which is anomalous and unexplained; (2) these rubric values come from a single verbatim pull at cycle 15 and have never been independently re-pulled, unlike the four TTP rows from the same table which have been confirmed twice. Cycle 18 added a third reason to be careful with them: the same 1.140 and 2.968 values, used as the third rung of an ordinal reading in another issue, normalise to 0.228 or 0.035 for GPT-4o and 0.594 or 0.492 for o3-mini depending on whether one divides by 5 or maps (x-1)/4, and the paper never states which -- so the rubric's absolute level is not interpretable, only its within-table contrasts are. Carry-forward [25] records that these values are not even present in state/knowledge/src-0007.md, living only in logs/cycle-015.md and issue prose. NOT RAISED TO 4, unchanged reason, now in its eighth cycle: open_question[2] asks whether src-0004's naming-convention hallucination is the same phenomenon as src-0002's quantified plausible-versus-correct gap or a distinct citation/naming-fabrication sub-type. That is the explicit alternative explanation for why these two sources sit in one issue, and no cycle has argued it either way. Level 4 requires counterarguments addressed, not articulated -- and this one is load-bearing, because if the ENISA error is a citation-fabrication sub-type then the issue's second leg is really evidence for institutional-incident-real-world-impact and this issue is closer to single-source than it looks. Also unchanged and not scored down on because it was already true at cycles 7, 10 and 13: the AI-causation of the ENISA leg rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise, and spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent (carry-forward [13]), so that leg cannot strengthen further without a source we cannot currently reach. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: RAISED 3 -> 4. This is the only score that moves this cycle and it is the one a successor should audit hardest, so the reasoning is given in full. IT MOVES BECAUSE THE ISSUE CHANGED, NOT BECAUSE THE EVIDENCE GOT A MORE GENEROUS READING. Six consecutive assessments (cycles 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13) recorded that this issue was being held DOWN artificially: a single score was being forced to average a narrow claim that cycle 13 called 'near-4' and 'about as well-evidenced as anything in this graph' against an ordinal axis that was actively disputed and worth 1-2, and every one of those cycles wrote that splitting the issue was the single highest-value structural change available to the graph precisely because it was the only thing that would let either half be scored honestly instead of averaged into a number describing neither. Cycle 16's T2 performed exactly that split. The ordinal axis, the cycle-2 candidate that carried it, and the open question about a better explanatory variable all moved verbatim to extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis, which is scored separately below. This issue now covers ONLY the narrow claim: that AI-generated CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property. Holding at 3 after the exact blocker was removed would mean the score never responds to the structural fix five cycles demanded, which is its own form of dishonesty. LEVEL 3 IS CLEARED EASILY. Two supported candidates rest on seven distinct sources from at least five unaffiliated teams: candidate 1 [src-0001, src-0002, src-0003, src-0005, src-0006], candidate 2 [src-0007, src-0013]. LEVEL 4 REQUIRES COUNTERARGUMENTS EXPLICITLY ADDRESSED, AND THE ONE THAT COULD SINK THIS ISSUE IS ADDRESSED BY CONSTRUCTION. open_question[3] asks whether the task-dependence conclusion would survive an independent replication showing a smaller IoC-extraction advantage -- i.e. whether the whole pattern is an artefact of leaning on src-0003's single-study, in-house, never-replicated LANCE result, which is additionally one side of the open contradiction ctr-0001. The answer is that it survives with src-0003 removed entirely, because the two strongest pieces of evidence here are WITHIN-STUDY designs that hold team, corpus, models and harness constant and vary only the sub-task, and neither involves src-0003. src-0007: the same four models on one expert-annotated production corpus reach IoC-extraction precision 0.8240-0.8846 while scoring 0.2787/0.2270 and 0.3480/0.1759 precision/recall on ATT&CK TTP identification, with GPT-4o at 1.140 out of 5 on the threat-actor Attribution rubric against 3.612 out of 5 for root-cause content in the same table -- roughly a 3x spread across sub-tasks with everything else fixed, every figure re-verified verbatim at cycle 15. src-0006: one corpus, one 15-model set, nine sub-tasks all in F1, spanning a true range of 0.286 to 0.882, re-pulled and re-derived independently at cycle 18. Cross-study synthesis can always be blamed on differing benchmarks; two within-study spreads cannot, and that is the specific counterargument-defeating property the rubric's level 4 is asking about. WHAT I CONSIDERED AS A COUNTERARGUMENT AND CONCLUDED IS NOT ONE. Cycle 18 derived from src-0006's nine commensurable rows that the mean between-MODEL range within a task (0.272) equals the mean between-TASK range within a model (0.263) to within 0.009, and recorded it as carry-forward [23]. It is tempting to read that as undercutting this issue. It does not: a mean between-task range of 0.263 within a single model, running as high as 0.404 for LL70 and 0.403 for LLY, is a direct CONFIRMATION that reliability varies sharply by sub-task. What it undercuts is the claim that sub-task is the PRIVILEGED explanatory variable, which is a claim this issue does not make and which lives in the child issue. Cycle 18 reached the same conclusion in [23] ('this does NOT negate the supported claim'). I record it here as a qualification rather than a demotion. I WAS GENUINELY TORN BETWEEN 3 AND 4 AND RESOLVED UPWARD ON A SUBSTANTIVE GROUND, NOT AN OPTIMISTIC ONE, so a successor can reverse it cleanly if it disagrees. The honest case for holding at 3 is that candidate 2 supplies the material that answers open_question[3] without ever CROSS-REFERENCING it, and 'explicitly addressed' can be read to require that a cycle join the two in the state rather than leaving a T4 to join them in a rationale -- the same strictness cycle 13 applied to ttp-attack-mapping-reliability when it refused to let a rationale create a three-source claim the graph did not record. I judged that candidate 2's construction IS the address rather than a raw ingredient, because its entire stated point is source-independence ('both of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task'), which is only responsive to the src-0003-replication worry. A successor that disagrees should drop this to 3 and say so. NOT 5, AND NOT CLOSE. Level 5 needs no material open questions and three remain, two of them substantive: whether human-in-the-loop validation specifically transfers to reasoning-heavy tasks (nobody has run a LANCE-style pipeline on ATT&CK mapping or attribution, searched for at cycle 6 and not found), and open_question[3] itself as literally posed, since no independent replication of src-0003 exists. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES CARRIED, DO NOT LET THEM BE STRIPPED: src-0013's leg of candidate 2 measures secure code generation, not CTI, and the candidate correctly flags this and defers to the cycle-16 scope ruling; src-0005 has never had a numeric value captured in the entire project (carry-forward [10]); candidate 1's prose still contains superseded ordinal-axis language ('the SPECIFIC ordinal axis ... is not confirmed by this evidence') that the cycle-16 split moved out of this issue, and a future T2 or T3 should annotate rather than delete it. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment.

extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis.rationale: FIRST SCORE EVER. Created cycle 16, never assessed -- discharging carry-forward [B], which had been carried unactioned for three cycles. SCORED ON EVIDENTIAL STATE, NOT ON THE POLARITY OF THE ANSWER. This issue's title question is now answered in the NEGATIVE: the ordinal ranking is not supported. A supported negative answer is an issue with a supported resolution, and the rubric is definitional -- 'a supported resolution exists' is the condition that matters, regardless of whether the resolution affirms or refutes the title. THE PRIMARY CANDIDATE IS SUPPORTED BY TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, from unaffiliated teams on different corpora with disjoint model sets, by two distinct routes. Route 1, src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows (one corpus, one 15-model set, one metric): Contextualization stage mean 0.636 (IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607) against Attribution stage mean 0.602 (TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511). The 0.034 gap is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best-performing task in the whole subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task -- so the ordering is not merely weak, it is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point. Route 2, src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models of the same family: GPT-4o's attribution rubric of 1.140/5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 against a derived TTP F1 of 0.2502 (at or below it), while o3-mini's 2.968/5 normalises to 0.594 or 0.492 against 0.2337 (above it), under both defensible normalisations, on a normalisation the paper never states. THE PROCEDURAL BLOCKER IS PROPERLY DISCHARGED AND I CHECKED THIS RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. The inherited cycle-16 open_question instructed that this issue 'should not rise above proposed' until a commensurable cross-sub-task measurement existed. Cycle 18 found one that had been sitting in this knowledge base since cycle 6 -- nine rows of src-0006's Table 2, all in F1, one corpus, one model set, spanning both ends of the proposed ordering -- so the condition is met on its own terms and the instruction no longer binds. It is marked SUPERSEDED in the issue text. Provenance is unusually good for a finding this young: cycle 17 pulled and recomputed the table, its state edits were reverted by the validator, and cycle 18 re-pulled from a second URL form and re-derived every mean, range and crossover independently rather than trusting the reverted arithmetic. WHY 3 AND NOT 4. Level 4 needs counterarguments addressed. The supported candidate states three material caveats and only one of them is actually addressed. (a) src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so the headline 0.034 carries NO uncertainty estimate at all -- stated, not addressed, and not addressable from any source in this base. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed order (carry-forward [22]); this one IS addressed, by a robustness check that drops all four and leaves 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) THE DECISIVE ONE: the fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so the candidate refutes the extraction-versus-classification-versus-attribution portion of a four-rung ordering and is explicitly SILENT on one quarter of the very ordering named in this issue's title. An issue whose supported resolution does not reach one of its own four rungs is not robust. Seven open_questions remain, two of them fundamental -- whether the 0.034 gap survives a second commensurable multi-sub-task study, and whether 0.034 is distinguishable from zero at all. WHY NOT 2, since I was torn and the standing instruction is to take the lower score when torn. I resolved to 3 because route 2 is not decorative: for a claim whose content is explicitly evidential ('the axis is NOT supported by the available commensurable measurement'), showing that the strongest apparent supporting source self-destructs on its own table is direct evidence for that claim, not merely absence of evidence. The honest case for 2 is that route 2 is DEFEATING evidence rather than CONFIRMING evidence, which would leave src-0006 alone carrying the claim and make this single-source. A successor that takes that view should drop it to 2 and say so. I also satisfied myself that the missing uncertainty estimate on 0.034 is not fatal to calling the candidate supported, because the candidate's claim survives without it: the local inversion (TTP Extraction at 0.673 beating every Contextualization task) is a qualitative fact about the printed table, not a significance question. THE THIRD CANDIDATE IS CORRECTLY 'proposed' AND CONTRIBUTES NOTHING TO THIS SCORE: model identity as the replacement explanatory variable, resting on the between-model 0.272 versus between-task 0.263 equality, which cycle 18 itself objects to on three grounds -- ranges are not variance components and are outlier-sensitive (LLY is an outlier on two of nine rows), the cross-source TTP comparison behind the corpus-identity limb is uncontrolled in at least four ways at once, and both figures come from one study's table. Its src-0014 limb (roughly fourfold spread in prompt-sensitivity between models, Gemma 0.398 against Mistral 0.103) was re-verified verbatim by this cycle's G2 and is exact; that confirms the citation, not the hypothesis. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment. SELECTOR NOTE: attempts are [17, 18], both inside the five-cycle penalty window, so this issue carries a tie-break penalty of 2 and should not be re-selected.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: HELD AT 3. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 12 -- attempts are [12], no source has been added, no candidate has changed status -- so this is a re-affirmation rather than a re-litigation, and the cycle-13 reasoning that raised it from 2 to 3 stands unamended. The existence claim is carried by candidate 2 with evidence [src-0009, src-0010, src-0004]: ENISA's OWN publication pages carrying verbatim revision notices against publication dates of 1 October 2025 and 6 November 2025, both revised 09 January 2026, corroborating report count, dates, defect type and correction date independently of the Der Spiegel/Heise chain that was previously the entire basis. And by candidate 3 with evidence [src-0012, src-0004]: a second named incident at a different institution type (EY Canada, 16 of 27 references hallucinated per GPTZero, report withdrawn), discovered by the identical route of an outside party clicking through footnotes. Two incidents at two institutions via two mutually independent investigations, plus the affected institution's own correction record, clears the level-3 bar. NOT RAISED TO 4, AND THE TWO REASONS ARE UNCHANGED AND BOTH STRUCTURAL. (a) THE BASE RATE IS UNMEASURED AND IS BLOCKED BY SCOPE, NOT BY EVIDENCE VOLUME. Two named incidents are two data points, not a rate, and open_question[0] asks for a rate across CTI publishers. src-0011 (GhostCite) is not that rate and its candidate is correctly 'proposed': it audits peer-reviewed conference papers, which have reviewers where CTI reports have none; it defines a ghost citation as one absent from any major academic database, largely inapplicable to CTI footnotes which are news and vendor URLs; it reports per-PAPER rates (1.01% of Security-venue papers containing at least one invalid citation) not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492; and its own authors call it a conservative lower bound. Treating a second anecdote plus an adjacent-population audit as a resolved base rate remains the most likely error available on this issue and it is not being made. (b) THE AI-CAUSATION LEG IS THE WEAKEST PART AND IT IS THE PART THE TOPIC IS ABOUT. For ENISA, AI attribution rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise (src-0004); ENISA's own pages assign no cause at all, spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent (carry-forward [13]), and every outlet repeating the 26-of-492 figure cites Der Spiegel, which is repetition rather than corroboration. For EY the 72% AI figure is the output of GPTZero's own commercial AI-detection product, so the load-bearing element there is the manually-checkable citation count. What is robustly established is that FABRICATED CITATIONS reached production at two named institutions; that AI CAUSED them is well-supported for EY and reported-but-not-primary for ENISA. ONE ITEM HARDENED SINCE CYCLE 13, recorded because it removes a 'pending' and replaces it with a permanent limit: carry-forward [14] establishes that the two ENISA v1.2 PDFs cannot be opened by this agent at all (no PDF text extraction exists on this runner -- poppler-utils, mutool, gs and qpdf are absent, the Read tool errors, and WebFetch returns undecoded bytes), so 'ENISA never disclosed the AI use' is established at landing-page level and is UNVERIFIABLE at document level here. Cycle 18 instructs that a T4 treat this as unestablished rather than pending, and I do. It does not lower the score, because the document-level claim is not what carries candidate 2, but it does mean this leg cannot strengthen. Three of five open_questions remain wholly or mostly open, and candidate 4 itself honestly concludes there is no single institutional response pattern to report -- an accurate non-answer on n=2, not a resolution. NO G3 ADJUSTMENT: no contradiction is filed against this issue, and cycle 12's reasoning for not opening one over ENISA's silence is endorsed -- the revision notices assign no cause at all, and silence is not a competing claim, so G3's 'two supported claims in conflict' is not met. Best available route to a 4 remains carry-forward [16]: GPTZero runs an automated pipeline over the right population and publishes findings one report at a time, which is the only lead any cycle has found that could produce a rate rather than another anecdote.

automated-triage-under-refusal.rationale: FIRST SCORE EVER. Created cycle 16, never assessed and never attempted (attempts is empty) -- discharging the second half of carry-forward [B]. THE FORMAL READING WOULD GIVE 3 AND IT IS WRONG. The issue has one candidate_resolution at status 'supported' with evidence [src-0007, src-0015], which on a mechanical count is two independent sources on the primary candidate. I scored it 2 because the state itself forbids that count. src-0015's own index entry records it as THE WEAKEST-PROVENANCE SOURCE IN THIS BASE and says in terms that it must not be the sole support for any candidate_resolution: single-author preprint filed cs.AI with no stated venue, peer review or affiliation; n = 40 synthetic RL-seed episodes per model from a 60-seed pool with no confidence intervals, so only the GPT-5.2-versus-Sonnet-4.5 contrast is robust and the middle two models' ordering is unresolved. The candidate itself agrees, stating that the claim RESTS on src-0007 and that src-0015 'is worth little as independent quantification'. Two sources of very unequal quality must not be allowed to read as two independent confirmations, so what this issue actually has is one load-bearing source plus a directional corroborator -- which is a 2 by the rubric's definition of partial evidencing. WHAT IS GENUINELY ESTABLISHED, and it is not nothing: src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026) measures automated triage on a real company's daily CTI workflow and reports recall (Accepted) of 0.90-1.00 against precision (Accepted) of 0.27-0.40 across all four models tested -- an extreme threshold asymmetry on production material from an institutionally affiliated, methodologically detailed source. src-0015 corroborates the direction on a different task and a newer model generation (GPT-5.2 containing in 100% of episodes at 82.5% false-positive rate, DeepSeek 3.2 92.5% at 65%, Gemini 3 75% at 57.5%, Claude Sonnet 4.5 62.5% at 45%, with evidence-gated action rates of 0.375-0.542), which is worth a great deal for showing the failure is not one benchmark's artefact and little as quantification. The issue's reason for existing is sound and is sharply stated by src-0015: 'All models correctly identify the ground-truth threat when they act; the calibration gap is not in detection but in restraint' -- these systems would score well on essentially every metric used elsewhere in this knowledge base and the defect is invisible to all of them. THE DECISIVE REASON THIS IS NOT 3: the issue's title question is not actually answered by its own supported candidate. open_questions[0], which the issue names as its central unknown, asks whether over-acceptance is a property of the MODELS or of the HARNESS -- and neither source varies the decision threshold, the stated cost of a false positive, the availability of an explicit abstain option, or the presence of a human confirmation step. The issue text concedes that until that experiment is run, 'the models under-refuse' and 'these harnesses were built with no refusal affordance' are INDISTINGUISHABLE. src-0003 already established for a different sub-task that scaffolding can dominate measured reliability, so this is a live alternative explanation, not a hypothetical one. All five open_questions are unaddressed, including whether any precision-recall frontier exists (nobody has published the precision these models reach at a recall of 0.7, so it is unknown whether this is a tuning problem or a capability problem) and what the operational cost actually is (src-0007's ground truth IS the human analyst's accept/reject decision, so by construction it carries no human error bar and cannot say whether human triage would score better on its own benchmark). VERIFICATION STATUS, STATED HONESTLY. src-0015 has NEVER been G2-verified, and its index URL is an /abs page -- which cycle 18 established carries no tables at all -- so its figures rest on a single abstract-page fetch. Cycle 15's G2 verified nine of src-0007's Table 4 rows verbatim to four decimal places, but those were the TTP and IoC rows; carry-forward [19] records that the full Triage pass-rate and bias rows from that same table are STILL UNCAPTURED, and it flags them as directly relevant here. So the one figure this issue's score rests on -- the 0.27-0.40 against 0.90-1.00 asymmetry -- has not itself been through a verbatim table pull. That is a real gap and it argues for 2 rather than 3 independently of the source-count argument. One pooling error to avoid, recorded at the candidate and repeated here: src-0015's 'calibration' is an action-threshold construct (false-positive rate, evidence-gating), NOT the ECE/Brier confidence calibration of src-0001 and src-0013, and the two must never be averaged or quoted as one measurement. No open contradiction, so no G3 adjustment. SELECTOR NOTE, AND IT IS THE OPERATIVE ONE THIS CYCLE: three issues sit at 2, but ioc-extraction-reliability was attempted at cycle 9 and consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode at cycles 3, 15 and 16 (a tie-break penalty of 2 for the two inside the five-cycle window), while THIS issue has an empty attempts array and has never received a single cycle of work. On the configured tie-break it is the unique weakest link.
